<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Epístola ad Romános
<r>Rom 14:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Infírmum autem in fide assúmite, non in disceptatiónibus cogitatiónum.
<n>2</n> Alius enim credit se manducáre ómnia: qui autem infírmus est, olus mandúcet.
<n>3</n> Is qui mandúcat, non manducántem non spernat: et qui non mandúcat, manducántem non iúdicet: Deus enim illum assúmpsit.
<n>4</n> Tu quis es, qui iúdicas aliénum servum? Dómino suo stat, aut cadit: stabit autem: potens est enim Deus statúere illum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Stella, quam víderant Magi in Oriénte, antecedébat eos, donec venírent ad locum, ubi puer erat.
* Vidéntes autem eam, gavísi sunt gáudio magno.
<r>℣.</r> Et intrántes domum, invenérunt púerum cum María matre eius, et procidéntes adoravérunt eum.
<r>℟.</r> Vidéntes autem eam, gavísi sunt gáudio magno.

<h>Reading 1</h>

<r>Rom 14:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Now him that is weak in faith, take unto you: not in disputes about thoughts.
<n>2</n> For one believeth that he may eat all things: but he that is weak, let him eat herbs.
<n>3</n> Let not him that eateth, despise him that eateth not: and he that eateth not, let him not judge him that eateth. For God hath taken him to him.
<n>4</n> Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? To his own lord he standeth or falleth. And he shall stand: for God is able to make him stand.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Benedictio.</r> In omni tribulatióne et angústia subvéniat nobis pia Virgo Maria.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Rom 14:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> Nam álius iúdicat diem inter diem, álius autem iúdicat omnem diem: unusquísque in suo sensu abúndet.
<n>6</n> Qui sapit diem, Dómino sapit. Et qui mandúcat, Dómino mandúcat: grátias enim agit Deo. Et qui non mandúcat, Dómino non mandúcat, et grátias agit Deo.
<n>7</n> Nemo enim nostrum sibi vivit, et nemo sibi móritur.
<n>8</n> Sive enim vívimus, Dómino vívimus: sive mórimur, Dómino mórimur. Sive ergo vívimus, sive mórimur, Dómini sumus.
<r>Rom 14:9-13</r>
<n>9</n> In hoc enim Christus mórtuus est, et resurréxit: ut et mortuórum et vivórum dominétur.
<n>10</n> Tu autem, quid iúdicas fratrem tuum? aut tu quare spernis fratrem tuum? Omnes enim stábimus ante tribúnal Christi.
<n>11</n> Scriptum est enim: Vivo ego, dicit Dóminus, quóniam mihi flectétur omne genu: et omnis lingua confitébitur Deo.
<n>12</n> Itaque unusquísque nostrum pro se ratiónem reddet Deo.
<n>13</n> Non ergo ámplius ínvicem iudicémus.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Venit lumen tuum, Ierúsalem, † et glória Dómini super te orta est :
* Et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, et reges in splendóre ortus tui.
<r>℣.</r> Fílii tui de longe vénient et fíliæ tuæ de látere surgent.
<r>℟.</r> Et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, et reges in splendóre ortus tui.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Rom 14:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> For one judgeth between day and day: and another judgeth every day: let every man abound in his own sense.
<n>6</n> He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord. And he that eateth, eateth to the Lord: for he giveth thanks to God. And he that eateth not, to the Lord he eateth not, and giveth thanks to God.
<n>7</n> For none of us liveth to himself; and no man dieth to himself.
<n>8</n> For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; or whether we die, we die unto the Lord. Therefore, whether we live, or whether we die, we are the Lord's.
<r>Rom 14:9-13</r>
<n>9</n> For to this end Christ died and rose again; that he might be Lord both of the dead and of the living.
<n>10</n> But thou, why judgest thou thy brother? or thou, why dost thou despise thy brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.
<n>11</n> For it is written: As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.
<n>12</n> Therefore every one of us shall render account to God for himself.
<n>13</n> Let us not therefore judge one another any more. But judge this rather, that you put not a stumblingblock or a scandal in your brother's way.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

<r>℟.</r> And the Gentiles shall walk in thy light, and kings in the brightness of thy rising.
b.0340b4acea:
<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Regína Angelórum.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
Ex Epístola sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi ad Sirícium Papam
<r>Epist. 81, alias 7, post initium</r>
<c>D</c>e via perversitátis prodúntur dícere: Virgo concépit, sed non virgo generávit. Pótuit ergo virgo concípere, non pótuit virgo generáre, cum semper concéptus præcédat, partus sequátur? Sed, si doctrínis non créditur sacerdótum, credátur oráculis Christi; credátur mónitis Angelórum dicéntium: Quia non est impossíbile Deo omne verbum; credátur Sýmbolo Apostolórum, quod Ecclésia Romána intemerátum semper custódit et servat. Audívit María vocem Angeli, et, quæ ante díxerat: Quómodo fiet istud; non de fide generatiónis intérrogans, respóndit póstea: Ecce ancílla Dómini, contíngat mihi secúndum verbum tuum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Virgo parens Christi, paritúra Deum genuísti: fúlgida stella maris, nos prótege, nos tueáris:
* Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Intercéde pia pro nobis Virgo María.
<r>℟.</r> Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.

<h>Reading 3</h>
From the letter of Blessed Ambrose, bishop of Milan, to Pope Siricius
<r>Epist. 81, alias 7</r>
<c>H</c>ow great is the madness of their dismal barkings, that the same persons should say that Christ could not be born of a virgin, and yet assert that women, after having given birth to human pledges, remain virgins? But if they will not believe the doctrines of the Clergy, let them believe the oracles of Christ, let them believe the admonitions of Angels who say, For with God nothing shall be impossible. Let them give credit to the Creed of the Apostles, which the Roman Church has always kept and preserved undefiled. Mary heard the voice of the Angel, and she who before had said “How shall this be?”, not asking from want of faith in the mode of generation, afterwards replied: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord, be it unto me according to thy word.”
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Virgo parens Christi, paritúra Deum genuísti: fúlgida stella maris, nos prótege, nos tueáris:
* Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Intercéde pia pro nobis Virgo María.
<r>℟.</r> Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>W</c>e praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.
All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.
To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.
To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.
<n>bow head</n> Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;
Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.
The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.
The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.
The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.
The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;
The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.
Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;
Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.
Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.
Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.
<n>During the following verse all make a profound bow:</n> When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.
When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.
We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.
<n>Kneel for the following verse</n> We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.
Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.
O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.
Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.
Day by day * we magnify thee;
<n>During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow.</n> And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.
O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.
O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.
O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uarto Idus Ianuárii Luna secúnda. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>n Thebáide natális beáti Pauli, primi Eremítæ, Confessóris, qui, a sextodécimo ætátis suæ anno usque ad centésimum décimum tértium, solus in erémo permánsit; cuius ánimam, inter Apostolórum et Prophetárum choros, ad cælum ferri ab Angelis sanctus Antónius vidit. Eius autem festívitas décimo octávo Kaléndas Februárii celebrátur.
<h>I</h>n Cypro beáti Nicánoris, qui fuit unus de septem primis Diáconis; atque, grátia fídei et virtúte admirándus, gloriosíssime coronátus est.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Agathónis Papæ, qui, sanctitáte et doctrína conspícuus, quiévit in pace.
<h>B</h>itúricis, in Aquitánia, sancti Willhélmi, Epíscopi et Confessóris, signis et virtútibus clari; quem Honórius Papa Tértius in Sanctórum cánonem adscrípsit.
<h>M</h>edioláni sancti Ioánnis Boni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sancti Marciáni Presbýteri.
<h>I</h>n monastério Cuxanénsi, in Gállia, natális sancti Petri Urséoli Confessóris, qui, ántea Venetiárum Dux et deínde Monáchus ex Ordine sancti Benedícti, pietáte et virtútibus cláruit.
<h>A</h>rétii, in Túscia, Beáti Gregórii Décimi, civis Placentíni, qui, ex Archidiácono Leodiénsi Summus Póntifex renuntiátus, Concílium Lugdunénse secúndum celebrávit, Græcísque ad unitátem fídei recéptis, compósitis Christianórum dissídiis, Terræ Sanctæ recuperatióne institúta, de universáli Ecclésia, quam sanctíssime gubernávit, óptime méritus est.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.60dadd3aa3:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>anuary 10th 2027, the 2nd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n the Thebaid, blessed Paul, the first Hermit, who from the sixteenth even unto the hundred and thirteenth year of his age dwelt alone in the desert, (in the year 342,) holy Anthony saw his soul borne heavenward by angels between the choirs of the Apostles and of the Prophets. We keep his feast upon the 15th day of this present month of January.
<h>I</h>n Cyprus, the blessed Nicanor, one of the seven first Deacons, who was wondrous for the grace of faith and power, and received a most glorious crown, (in the year 35 or 76.)
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy Pope Agatho, who was eminent for holiness and learning, and fell asleep in peace, (in the year 682.)
<h>A</h>t Bourges, in Aquitaine, (in the year 1209,) the holy Confessor William, Archbishop (of that see,) famous for signs and works of power, whose name Honorius III enrolled with those of the saints.
<h>A</h>t Milan, the holy Confessor John, surnamed the Good, Archbishop of that city, (in the year 659.)
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy Priest Marcian, (about the year 489.)
<h>I</h>n the monastery of Cusan, (in the diocese of Perpignan,) the holy Confessor Peter Urseoli, who was sometime Doge of Venice, and then became a monk of the Order of St. Benedict, and was famous for godliness and works of power, (in the year 997.)
<h>A</h>t Arezzo, in Tuscany, [in the year 1276,] the blessed Pope Gregory X he was a man of Piacenza, and was raised to the Supreme Pontificate from the arch-deaconry [of Liege.]
<h>H</h>e held the Second Council of Lyon, received the Greeks into the unity of the faith, healed the dissensions of Christendom, set forward the recovery of the Holy Land, and governed the Church in holiness.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Luc 2:51</r>
<c>D</c>escéndit Iesus cum María et Ioseph, et venit Názareth: et erat súbditus illis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Descéndit Iesus cum paréntibus, et venit Názareth: et erat súbditus illis. Et Mater eius conservábat ómnia verba hæc in corde suo.
* Et Iesus proficiébat sapiéntia et ætáte et grátia apud Deum et hómines.
<r>℣.</r> Honóra patrem tuum et matrem tuam: sic præcéperat Dóminus Deus in Lege Móysi, et ita in Fílio suo exémplum nobis præbuit.
<r>℟.</r> Et Iesus proficiébat sapiéntia et ætáte et grátia apud Deum et hómines.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Et Iesus proficiébat sapiéntia et ætáte et grátia apud Deum et hómines.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>O</c> lux beáta cǽlitum
Et summa spes mortálium,
Iesu, o cui doméstica
Arrísit orto cáritas:

<h>M</h>aría, dives grátia,
O sola quæ casto potes
Fovére Iesum péctore,
Cum lacte donans óscula:

<h>T</h>uque ex vetústis pátribus
Delécte custos Vírginis
Dulci patris quem nómine
Divína Proles ínvocat:

<h>D</h>e stirpe Iesse nóbili
Nati in salútem géntium,
Audíte nos qui súpplices
Vestras ad aras sístimus.

<h>D</h>um sol redux ad vésperum
Rebus nitórem détrahit,
Nos hic manéntes íntimo
Ex corde vota fúndimus.

<h>Q</h>ua vestra sedes flóruit
Virtútis omnis grátia,
Hanc detur in domésticis
Reférre posse móribus.

<h>I</h>esu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Beáti qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine.
<r>℟.</r> In sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.

Whose breast gave milk to Jesus,
Whose arms thy God embraced;

<h>A</h>nd thou of all men chosen
To guard the Virgin’s fame,
To whom God’s Son refused not
A Father’s gracious name;

<h>B</h>orn for the nation’s healing,
Of Jesse’s lineage high,
Behold the suppliants kneeling,
O hear the sinners’ cry!

<h>T</h>he sun returned to evening,
Dusks all the twilight air:
We, lingering here before you,
Pour out our heartfelt prayer.

<h>Y</h>our home was as a garden
Made glad with fairest flowers;
May life thus blossom sweetly
In every home of ours.

<h>A</h>ll praise to Thee, O Jesus,
who parents dost obey;
Praise to the sovereign Father
and Paraclete for aye.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord.
<r>℟.</r> They shall praise thee for ever and ever.

b.4679a9bcc1:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>ómine Iesu Christe, qui, Maríæ et Ioseph súbditus, domésticam vitam ineffabílibus virtútibus consecrásti: fac nos, utriúsque auxílio, Famíliæ sanctæ tuæ exémplis ínstrui; et consórtium cónsequi sempitérnum:
<h>Q</h>ui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.b9fbc44675:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>L</c>ord Jesus Christ, who subject to Mary and Joseph, didst consecrate family life by thy unspeakable virtues, aid us by their united intercession to profit by the examples of thy Holy Family, and attain to their everlasting companionship:
<h>W</h>ho livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
